title: Set a sand core in its prints, then close the cope between the guide posts
instruction: Set the grey core in the mould with each end on its ledge, then lower the blue cope flat between the posts.
context: Closing a sand mould is the last step before pouring: a core left proud or a cocked cope scraps the casting. Done by foundry mould and coremakers (O*NET 51-4071.00). Closest board tasks, the access panel with retainer bars and the stacked avionics covers, seat flat parts; here a 26 cm bar goes down a 4 cm slot, then a 31 cm cover hides it, and a cope closed over no core or an unseated core scores 0.
setup: Sizes are x by y by height. Positions are object centres in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left. Table: wood top, arm bases 61 cm apart (y +30.5 and -30.5) on its near edge; nothing else on it. Drag, fixed, dark brown wood, 5 cm tall: two walls 1.5 x 31 cm at x 19.25 and x 24.75, y 0, leaving a 4 cm wide cavity between them (x 20 to 24); two end blocks 4 x 1.5 cm at x 22, y +14.75 and -14.75; two print ledges 4 x 2.5 x 1 cm at x 22, y +12.75 and -12.75 (the prints). Guide posts: four black wood posts, 1.5 x 1.5 x 9 cm, at x 16.75 and 27.25, y +17.25 and -17.25. Core: light grey rigid foam bar, 2.5 x 26 x 4 cm (long side along y), 80 g, centre x 32, y 0, lying on two mid-green wood rests 4 x 4 x 1 cm at x 32, y +8 and -8. Cope: blue painted wood bar, 7 x 31 x 3 cm (long side along y), 400 g, centre x 12.5, y 0, on two mid-green wood rests 5 x 5 x 2 cm at x 12.5, y +9 and -9. Seated, the core spans y -13 to +13 (1 cm of play at each end, 0.75 cm to each wall) and its top is level with the drag top; the closed cope is 1 cm clear of every post.
scoring: Open both grippers, measure the cope (height at both ends, outline against the posts), then lift it off and measure the core. CORE SEATED: centre x 20.5 to 23.5 and within 1.2 cm of y 0, underside within 0.4 cm of 1 cm above the table, tilt at most 3 degrees (1.4 cm difference between its ends). COPE CLOSED: outline inside the four posts (x 17.5 to 26.5, y -16.5 to 16.5), underside within 0.25 cm of 5 cm at both ends, tilt at most 2 degrees (0.24 cm difference across its 7 cm width). Either face of either part may be up. 1.0: both, at rest, hands clear of the cope. 0.7: core seated, cope inside the posts but proud or tilted. 0.5: core seated, cope anywhere else. 0.2: core in the cavity (x 20.5 to 23.5, within 2 cm of y 0), underside at most 2 cm above the table, not seated, cope not closed. Otherwise 0, including a cope closed over an unseated core, or either part more than 2 cm below the table top (off the table), whatever else holds. A moving part counts as not placed. Pushing cannot score: the drag's 5 cm wall stops both parts.
reset_notes: Lay the core and the cope back on their rests, and brush any loose grit off the ledges and the drag top. The drag, posts and rests stay fixed.
fidelity: Approximate: rigid boxes with default friction; a real core is fragile and a real cope has pin holes, neither scored. The simulator scores the last step with the grippers still closed, so a part whose bottom is more than 1 cm above every support counts as not placed, and a cope with a gripper within 2 cm of it counts as not released.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (moved the right arm over the table, never lifted the core or cope); demo: 1.0 (set the core in the drag, then lowered the blue cope between the posts)
